title: POC Weekly Sync - Quality Eval
summary: Weekly POC sync to review quality eval results for prompt set v2, discuss regressions, tuning options (prompt edits, reranking, safety guardrails), and next steps for private deployment benchmarking and security docs.
next_steps: Redwood: share tuned prompt set v3 and eval spreadsheet by 2025-08-07
Acme: run internal regression tests on v2 edge cases and share failing prompts by 2025-08-08
Both: schedule latency benchmark for private deployment week of 2025-08-12
Redwood: send SOC2 and security checklist link
action_items: Jordan Lee: send pricing + security deck (SOC2 link) by 2025-08-07
Priya Patel: produce prompt set v3 and run evals, share spreadsheet by 2025-08-07
Ben O'Neill: confirm VPC peering constraints and existing KMS details by 2025-08-08
Samir Joshi: assemble failing prompts list and upload to drive by 2025-08-08
transcript:
Header: 2025-08-05 10:00 UTC | Duration: 55m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marta (Redwood CSM), Carlos (Acme Head of ML), Aisha (PM), Ben (Infra), Samir (DS)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, good to see you all. agenda is quick review of the v2 evals, look at the regressions Carlos flagged, and decide next steps for tuning and the private benchmark.
[00:18] Carlos: yep thanks, we've got about 30 mins of results to go through, then the infra questions. we've seen a drop in accuracy on the product-summarization prompts, and a weird hallucination case on the support-response set.
[00:35] Priya: ok, quick context \u0014 these evals are the 5k prompt set you provided, with scoring weighted for factuality 0.6, relevance 0.3, tone 0.1, correct?
[00:46] Samir: right, we used the same rubric as last week, but we did add the new negative examples to stress guardrails.
[00:55] Jordan: perfect. Marta, i'll let you note action items if anything pops up.
[01:05] Marta: noted.
[01:12] Priya: diving in \u0014 overall the mean score for v2 is 0.78, which is a small bump from v1 at 0.75, but the std dev increased and there are ~120 outliers below 0.5. most of those are in two buckets: 1) long product specs where the model hallucinates specs, 2) multi-turn support threads where the model drops context.
[01:34] Carlos: the hallucinations worry us because they affect trust. we feed these into customer-facing summaries. we caught one where it invented a warranty term.
[01:44] Priya: we looked at those with the debugging tool \u0014 a couple of patterns: the system prompt was a bit permissive on creativity for those templates, and the prefix KV caching (we saw references to 'KV cash' in notes, haha) \u0014 when the cache hits were high, generation sometimes pulled stale tokens.
[02:05] Ben: wait, stale tokens? is that a runtime issue or our prompt handling?
[02:12] Priya: more prompt + runtime interplay. the runtime uses prefix caching to speed repeated prompts; in the POC config we had an aggressive cache TTL which can cause context mixing if the prompt scaffolding isn't unique per request. we can fix by namespacing the prompt or reducing TTL.
[02:30] Carlos: ok that makes sense. can you confirm that changing TTL won't impact latency too much?
[02:38] Priya: should be a small impact, we measured a 5-10% token throughput hit in similar setups. but for accuracy it's worth it. on the multi-turn drop, we saw the KV cache and batching interactions \u0014 with high batching the model drops older chat turns beyond the LRU window.
[02:58] Samir: so tradeoff is latency/cost vs fidelity. we noted that in the eval sheet. link: https://drive.example.com/acme/poc/results-v2.csv (shared)
[03:10] Jordan: let's mark that as an action: Priya to produce a mode run with conservative caching + smaller batch window and rerun the failing subset.
[03:20] Priya: will do.
[03:26] Aisha: on the guardrails side, we tried the built-in safety filter but we saw false positives on benign legal language \u0014 it flagged certain warranty phrases. is there a way to tune the sensitivity?
[03:38] Priya: yes, we can tune thresholds and add allow-lists for domain-specific tokens. also adding a reranker focusing on factuality helps since filter is binary. reranker will score candidates and pick lower hallucination chance.
[03:50] Carlos: how much latency does reranking add?
[03:55] Priya: depends on candidate count. with a 3-candidate rerank it's ~30-50ms median overhead in our hosted infra, could be higher in private depending on infra. if latency is tight we can do lightweight heuristics or run rerank asynchronously and fallback.
[04:12] Ben: for private, our big ask is KMS integration and no outbound connections. is Redwood Private able to run fully air-gapped?
[04:22] Jordan: yes, our Private deployment can be on-prem or in a VPC with no egress. we support customer KMS/HSM integration (we did a similar setup with RetailCo last quarter). we'll share the SOC2 and deployment checklist. redwood soc2 link: https://redwood.example.com/soc2.pdf
[04:39] Ben: great \u0014 and SAML SSO for admin? we need RBAC.
[04:44] Marta: yes SAML SSO and role-based access is supported; we can include the admin flow and audit log export example.
[04:52] Aisha: back to quality \u0014 you mentioned scoring weights. can we tweak thresholds to reduce hallucination pass-through?
[04:59] Priya: absolutely. we can upweight factuality and add a hard reject for hallucination signals. also add extra system prompt constraints: do not invent warranty or pricing info, only cite from product spec block.
[05:12] Carlos: hmm, that may help but we worry about over-constraining tone. some marketing copy needs creativity.
[05:20] Jordan: split traffic: use a routing policy \u0014 high-trust prompts go to conservative model configs, marketing prompts go to a more creative profile. that's what Redwood routing supports \u0014 canary by route, model variant.
[05:35] Samir: can we see latency/cost tradeoff estimates for both profiles?
[05:40] Priya: yes \u0014 i'll add an example table to the spreadsheet.
[05:44] Jordan: on regressions specifically \u0014 Carlos flagged a 12% drop in factuality on product-summarization. do we have one or two failing examples live?
[05:55] Carlos: yes i pulled three; here's one: prompt id 3, the model added a 2-year warranty when none exists.
[06:03] Priya: ok that's classic hallucination. i'll run prompt-edits: 1) add explicit spec block to system prompt, 2) add a do-not-invent statement, 3) enforce citation requirement. we'll push v3 prompt set.
[06:17] Aisha: will those edits change token counts much? our cost model is token sensitive.
[06:22] Priya: slightly \u0014 adding spec blocks increases context tokens but we can compress by referencing id tokens and using embeddings to fetch relevant spec chunk at inference time. that reduces full-token context.
[06:34] Ben: embeddings + retrieval is more infra, any latency penalties?
[06:38] Priya: sub-100ms for retrieval in our config, depends on index size and vector DB. for private we recommend hosting the index locally.
[06:46] Jordan: good note \u0014 Ben, can you confirm if you can run a small vector DB instance in your VPC?
[06:51] Ben: yes we can. we'll coordinate on sizing.
[06:55] Marta: action item: Ben to confirm vector DB sizing by 2025-08-08. noted.
[07:02] Samir: quick question on eval scoring \u0014 are we using automatic metrics or human-in-the-loop?
[07:07] Priya: both. majority auto with a sampled human check for borderline cases. for the failing set we did human review which confirmed hallucinations.
[07:18] Carlos: can we tune the auto scorer to be stricter on factuality?
[07:22] Priya: yes, change threshold from 0.6 to 0.7 will reduce false passes but may increase false negatives. we'll show the precision/recall tradeoff in the sheet.
[07:32] Jordan: ok next up, the regression timeline \u0014 if Priya ships v3 prompts by Thu (2025-08-07) and we rerun the failing 120 prompts, what's a reasonable turnaround?
[07:45] Priya: rerun subset is quick, we can get results same day in hosted; private may take longer depending on Ben's infra \u0014 but estimate 24-48 hours once config is up.
[07:56] Ben: for private we'll need a maintenance window to deploy a config change, maybe next Tue.
[08:02] Jordan: fine, we'll plan around that.
[08:08] Aisha: another concern \u0014 the false positives from safety filter mean some good replies are dropped; do you support a review queue for filtered outputs?
[08:18] Priya: yes, you can ship filtered outputs to a review queue with metadata and the reranker result so a human can audit and accept. we can demo that.
[08:27] Carlos: excellent. that helps adoption.
[08:31] Samir: i pulled some debug traces \u0014 there are a few times where speaker attribution in our transcripts is off, like Speaker 2 labeled as \"Customer\". unrelated but noticed transcription quality is medium.
[08:44] Jordan: noted, not critical for model eval but good call-out.
[08:48] Priya: quick tech note: we also found one case where tokenization split a trademark token differently causing the model to mis-associate spec fields. tokenization mismatch across tokenizer versions can cause subtle bugs. make sure your tokenizer matches the model artifact.
[09:06] Carlos: ouch. we'll check versioning.
[09:10] Jordan: ok i'm going to summarize the concrete plan: Priya will produce prompt set v3 with three variants: conservative (no invention), balanced (mild creativity), creative (marketing). she'll run v3 on the failing subset with conservative config and post results. Priya will also run a cache-conservative config.
[09:28] Priya: yes, and i'll include reranker-on and reranker-off comparisons, and include latency/cost estimates for hosted vs private.
[09:35] Jordan: Marta will send the SOC2 + deployment checklist and the SAML/RBAC docs. i'll include a case study for RetailCo.
[09:43] Marta: sending after call.
[09:45] Ben: one more infra question \u0014 does Redwood Private support restricted egress only to our internal KMS? we need to ensure HSM integration patterns.
[09:55] Jordan: yes, we support customer-managed KMS/HSM and can integrate via the standard KMIP or cloud KMS approaches. we'll include architecture notes.
[10:05] Aisha: about routing \u0014 could we do A/B test on a 10% creative vs 90% conservative for a week?
[10:12] Jordan: absolutely, Redwood Console supports A/B route rollouts and automatic fallback to conservative on errors. we'll include instructions.
[10:20] Carlos: timeline question \u0014 assuming prompts v3 fixes, when can we move to a limited production pilot?
[10:26] Priya: depends on infra readiness; realistically 2-3 weeks after we lock on config and pass regressions.
[10:34] Jordan: ok that's fine.
[10:37] Marta: quick recap and next steps \u0014 i will: 1) send SOC2 doc + deployment checklist (Jordan/RW to attach case study) by 2025-08-07, 2) Priya to share prompt set v3 and eval spreadsheet by 2025-08-07, 3) Ben to confirm VPC peering and vector DB sizing by 2025-08-08, 4) Samir/Carlos to upload failing prompts and any additional edge cases by 2025-08-08, 5) schedule latency benchmark for private deployment week of 2025-08-12.
[10:56] Jordan: perfect \u0014 any other questions?
[11:00] Carlos: none, thanks everyone.
[11:02] Jordan: thanks, we'll follow up in email with links and the sheet. meeting adjourned.

References/Artifacts: results csv: https://drive.example.com/acme/poc/results-v2.csv, redwood soc2: https://redwood.example.com/soc2.pdf, demo deck: https://drive.example.com/acme/poc/demo-deck.pdf

Transcript notes: occasional transcription errors (names, KV cache noted as KV cash), some speaker labels simplified.
